claims.text: Reported HfNbTiVAl10 has an inherent hierarchical heterostructure.
A physics-informed machine-learning model can predict Young’s modulus in HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
The model can predict yield strength in HfNbTiVAl10 under tensile testing.
The model can predict fracture-related behavior or parameters in HfNbTiVAl10.
The model will reduce prediction error by approximately 15–20% relative to established simulation methods.
The model will generate predictions approximately 10 times faster than established simulation methods.
The proposed model will use descriptors of grain-boundary networks, secondary-phase distributions, and nanoscale heterogeneities.
The framework will be trained and calibrated using in situ imaging, extracted features, tensile and fracture data, and selected high-fidelity simulations.
Detailed microstructural descriptors constrain the model’s physical parameter space.
Structural heterogeneity influences the mechanical response of high-entropy alloys.
Encoding the influence of structural heterogeneity enables faster convergence to accurate mechanical-property predictions.
Established simulation approaches do not explicitly represent the hierarchical heterostructure’s multiscale microstructural details.
Established simulations are less accurate than the proposed model for this prediction task.
Established simulations are slower than the proposed model for this prediction task.
Unexpected phase transformations or environmental influences may dominate tensile and fracture behavior and cause the model to fail.
Model performance may be sensitive to the quality of microstructural feature extraction.
The proposed validation covers room-temperature and elevated-temperature tensile and fracture regimes.
A descriptor–property association with p-value greater than 0.05 is a predeclared falsification outcome.
Failure to achieve at least a 15% accuracy improvement is a predeclared falsification outcome.
Failure to achieve a 10-fold computation-time reduction is a predeclared falsification outcome.
